fine_lines.title: inconvenient vs inconvenience
fine_lines.explanation_ar: inconvenient صفة: It was inconvenient. أما inconvenience فاسم: sorry for the inconvenience.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Inconvenient" is an adjective; "inconvenience" is a noun.

examples.sentence: It must have been very inconvenient for you.
We are sorry for the inconvenience.

fine_lines.title: I'm sorry to hear that vs I'm sorry for
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I'm sorry to hear that تُظهر التعاطف عندما يخبرك أحد بمشكلة. أما I'm sorry for + اسم/‑ing فتعتذر عن شيء فعلته أنت أو شركتك.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I'm sorry to hear that" shows sympathy for someone's news. "I'm sorry for + noun/-ing" apologises for something you did.

examples.sentence: Your order was late? I'm really sorry to hear that.
I'm sorry for sending the wrong file.

expressions.phrase: I'm really sorry to hear that.
expressions.meaning_en: Show you are sorry about someone's problem.
expressions.example: Your delivery didn't arrive? I'm really sorry to hear that.

expressions.meaning_en: Agree that the mistake is very bad.
expressions.example: Sending the wrong goods is totally unacceptable.

expressions.phrase: It must have been very inconvenient for you.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا بدّ أن ذلك كان مزعجًا جدًا لك.
expressions.meaning_en: Show you understand the problem it caused.
expressions.example: Waiting all day must have been very inconvenient for you.

expressions.phrase: You have my word that we will sort this out.
expressions.example: You have my word that we will sort this out by Friday.

expressions.phrase: We could include ... to make up for the inconvenience.
expressions.meaning_ar: يمكننا أن نضيف ... تعويضًا عن الإزعاج.
expressions.meaning_en: Offer something extra to make the customer happy.
expressions.example: We could include free delivery to make up for the inconvenience.

expressions.phrase: I promise you, it won't happen again.
expressions.meaning_en: Promise the mistake will not happen again.
expressions.example: I'm very sorry. I promise you, it won't happen again.

expressions.phrase: I look forward to working with you.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite ending with a client.
expressions.example: Thank you, Mr Lime. I look forward to working with you.

grammar.title: must have + past participle
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم must have + التصريف الثالث لنستنتج شيئًا عن الماضي بثقة: It must have been very inconvenient (أنا متأكد تقريبًا أنه كان مزعجًا).
grammar.explanation_en: Use "must have + past participle" to say you are almost sure about something in the past.
examples: It must have been very inconvenient for you.
You must have been very angry.
The driver must have taken the wrong box.

grammar.title: Steps of a good apology
grammar.explanation_ar: الاعتذار الجيد في العمل له خطوات: 1) قل إنك آسف: I'm really sorry to hear that. 2) اعترف بالمشكلة: That's totally unacceptable. 3) أظهر التفهّم: It must have been inconvenient. 4) عِد بالحل: You have my word... 5) قدّم تعويضًا وعِد بعدم التكرار.
grammar.explanation_en: A good work apology has steps: 1) say sorry, 2) accept the problem, 3) show you understand, 4) promise to fix it, 5) offer something extra and promise it won't happen again.
examples: I'm really sorry to hear that.
You have my word that we will sort this out.
I promise you, it won't happen again.
